summary.text: Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer, physicist, engineer and polymath, born in Pisa, who has been called the father of observational astronomy and modern science.
With an improved telescope he built, he observed the phases of Venus, the four largest satellites of Jupiter, Saturn's rings, lunar craters and sunspots.
His championing of Copernican heliocentrism met opposition from the Catholic Church, and the Inquisition forced him to recant and he spent the rest of his life under house arrest.

facts.label: Birthplace
facts.value: Pisa, then part of the Duchy of Florence

facts.label: 1615 inquiry
facts.value: The Roman Inquisition investigated his heliocentrism

facts.label: Late book
facts.value: Two New Sciences, 1638, on kinematics and materials' strength

facts.label: Other instruments
facts.value: Early developer of the thermoscope; built an early microscope

items.prompt: In church, young Galileo timed a chandelier swinging in bigger and smaller arcs against his pulse. What did he find?

options.label: Each swing took about the same time, whatever the width
Wider swings took clearly longer than narrow ones
Narrower swings took clearly longer than wide ones
Swing time depended on how long the chandelier hung

items.explain: He noticed the chandelier seemed to take the same time per swing however far it swung, and two pendulums of equal length kept time together.

items.prompt: The pope and the Jesuits had long supported Galileo. What turned them against him before his trial?

options.label: A paper attacking Aristotle's physics
A refusal to appear before the Inquisition in 1615
A book that appeared to dispute and satirize the pope
A claim that the Bible contained no astronomy

items.explain: His Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems appeared to dispute and satirize Pope Urban VIII, alienating both the pope and the Jesuits.

items.prompt: After his trial, what did Galileo do with his remaining years?

options.label: Left Italy for good to lecture at universities abroad
Lived under house arrest and wrote on kinematics and materials
Served a long prison term and was barred from writing
Returned to Pisa to teach medicine to young students

items.explain: He spent the rest of his life under house arrest and during that time wrote the Two New Sciences, about kinematics and the strength of materials.

items.prompt: What may have pushed young Galileo toward inventions that could bring extra income?

options.label: A prize offered by the Duke of Florence
A large inheritance he wished to invest
Pressure from the Church to build instruments
Family money troubles, such as his brother's debts and sisters' dowries

items.explain: His brother Michelangelo added to his financial burdens, as did dowry problems with his sisters, and these may have contributed to his early desire to invent.

items.prompt: Galileo seriously considered the priesthood as a young man. What did he do instead, at his father's urging?

options.label: Enrolled at the University of Pisa for a medical degree
Became a lutenist and composer like his father
Joined the Vallombrosa Abbey as a monk
Studied law in Florence

items.explain: At his father's urging he enrolled at the University of Pisa for a medical degree.

items.prompt: In 1615 the Roman Inquisition investigated Galileo's championing of heliocentrism. What did it conclude?

options.label: That his telescope observations were faulty or invented
That he had copied his claims from another astronomer
That his opinions contradicted accepted Biblical interpretations
That he must at once be put under house arrest

items.explain: The Inquisition concluded that his opinions contradicted accepted Biblical interpretations. His trial and house arrest came after the 1632 Dialogue.
